_note: Scripted replay of the exception agent's turns (text + tool calls). Tools, policy and ETAs are computed live by the app on every run. Replace this file with a recorded live run: npm run scenario -- --record

initial.text: Closure north of Albury. First: what do the reports say, which loads are exposed, and what relief capacity do we have?

Closure estimate. The reports conflict: the road authority says 'until further notice', police on site say 3–4h, and creek levels peak around 02:00 (4h20m from now). Floodwater roads usually reopen after the peak plus an inspection, so I'm planning on 5h, low confidence. Wodonga has only 2 relief drivers (D-M3 can't be there before 01:10), and 4 loads are affected. D-A1 on the perishable load has just 2.0h left, and the DG load can't use the Olympic detour. Evaluating each load under the 5h assumption.

Allocation. Only the Olympic detour with a fresh driver gets L-1042 (A$9,000 write-off at 06:00) and L-1038 (A$2,500 penalty at 06:00) in on time: 05:13 and 04:55. Waiting for the Hume misses both windows if the closure lasts 5h. So both Wodonga relief drivers go to those two. L-1051 is DG: Olympic is banned, so hold at Wodonga and rest the driver 7h; it leaves at 04:40 and arrives 09:52 against a 10:00 window, which only slips if the closure runs past 04:40 (7h). L-1060 has a flexible 14:00 window: rest at Wodonga, no relief driver needed. Expected cost of this plan: A$0 if the Hume reopens within ~5h.

input.rationale: Reports conflict (authority: until further notice; police: 3–4h; creek peak 02:00), so I planned on a 5h closure. Both Wodonga relief drivers go to the two loads with costed 06:00 windows (perishable A$9,000, retail penalty A$2,500) via the Olympic detour. The DG load can't use Olympic, so it holds at Wodonga; 09:52 vs 10:00 is tight and slips if the closure runs past 04:40. The flexible load rests at Wodonga.

initial.text: Two holds executed under policy; the two driver swaps are with the dispatcher. Notifying the customer whose window is at risk.

input.message: The Hume is closed by flooding north of Albury and your load can't take the detour. It's holding safely at our Wodonga hub and is planned to arrive about 09:50, just inside your 10:00 window. If the road is still closed at about 04:30 we'll call you to rebook.

replan.text: D-W2 is gone, so L-1038 has no driver. Who else could take it, and is it worth moving D-W1 off the perishable load?

L-1038 will be late whatever we do: D-M3 can't reach Wodonga before 01:35. Swapping D-W1 onto L-1038 would save the A$2,500 penalty but put L-1042 late, a A$9,000 write-off, so D-W1 stays on the perishable load. For L-1038 with D-M3: Hume 08:17 only if the road reopens by ~03:05; Olympic 08:44 doesn't depend on the flood. Same penalty either way, and confidence in the reopening is low, so I'm taking the certain ETA.

input.rationale: D-W2 dropped out. Moving D-W1 to this load would trade a A$2,500 penalty for a A$9,000 perishable write-off, so D-W1 stays. D-M3 drives up from Melbourne (at Wodonga 01:35) and takes L-1038 via the Olympic Hwy: 08:44, late, A$2,500 penalty. The Hume option (08:17) depends on the road reopening by ~03:05, which is low confidence.

replan.text: Telling Northline now rather than at 06:00.

input.message: Flooding has closed the Hume near Albury. Your replenishment load will arrive about 08:45 instead of before 06:00, with a fresh driver via the inland route. Sorry for the delay; please let us know if you need a different unloading slot.
